name: Austria
summary: Children and the spouse are guaranteed half of their intestate share (Pflichtteil), and a will cannot remove it. A foreign national habitually resident in Austria can choose the law of their nationality under the EU Succession Regulation. Austria has no trust law, but a Privatstiftung (private foundation) can be set up under the PSG.
reserved_share: Descendants and spouse or registered partner: a Pflichtteil of half their statutory share, paid in money (ABGB sections 756-759; parents and other ascendants no longer protected since the 2017 reform).
foreign_law_note: Reg. 650/2012 art. 22 lets a person choose the law of their nationality for the whole estate; without a choice, the law of last habitual residence applies (art. 21). A choice of foreign law removes the Austrian Pflichtteil, subject to the public-policy exception (art. 35).
trust_note: Austria has no domestic trust law and is not party to the Hague Trusts Convention. The HCCH status table lists no signature or ratification for this state; the Convention is not in force here. Foreign trusts are treated in practice as contractual or fiduciary arrangements. Transfers to a Privatstiftung (Privatstiftungsgesetz 1993) are taxed under the Stiftungseingangssteuergesetz, which also reaches comparable foreign foundations.
open_questions: Austrian tax treatment of foreign trusts (Stiftungseingangssteuergesetz scope, income tax on distributions) was not examined in detail.
Exact ABGB section numbers for the 2017 Pflichtteil rules were taken from memory plus general guides and should be checked at ris.bka.gv.at.
